why: The servers sit on a ring, and visiting a set of points on a ring means walking an arc that covers them all. Sort the positions; the walk can skip exactly one gap between neighbouring targets (including the wrap-around gap), so skip the largest one: answer = total_servers - largest gap.
hints: Draw the ring with the target servers marked. Any walk that touches them all covers one continuous arc. Which part of the ring does it leave out?
Walking in one direction from the right start point covers everything except one gap between two consecutive targets. Leave out the biggest gap.
Sort and dedupe servers, compute the gaps pts[i]-pts[i-1] and the wrap gap pts[0]+total_servers-pts[-1], and return total_servers minus the maximum. O(n log n), independent of total_servers.
pitfalls: Do not forget the wrap-around gap from the last server back to the first (example 2: servers 1 and 5 on a ring of 5 are adjacent).
Duplicates or a single distinct server give answer 0.
total_servers can be 10^9, so never build an array over the ring.
